checkpoint_text: Check for scratches, scuffs, and drag marks, even using magnification if necessary.
Assess sink marks for their depth and frequency.
Identify flow lines and weld lines and note their impact on appearance or integrity.
Look for burn marks and discoloration, especially near gates and edges.
Verify uniform gloss or matte finish across the entire part.
Ensure no foreign particles (dust, debris) are embedded in or adhering to surfaces.
Confirm no blotches or cloudiness affecting even coloration.
Check for flash around holes, slots, and external contours that might hinder assembly.
Ensure no visible trimming or cutting marks on external surfaces.
Parting lines should be clean, well-defined, with no excess material.
Inspect all edges for burrs or roughness that pose safety risks or interfere with fit.
Confirm edges match design intent (sharp or rounded as specified).
Look for cracks and fractures; gently flex the part if safe to detect hidden weaknesses.
Identify voids or air bubbles that may compromise structural strength.
Check thick-walled areas for shrinkage-related defects or inconsistent density.
Look for signs of delamination (layered or peeling surfaces) indicating poor bonding.
Ensure the part is not unexpectedly brittle or overly rigid.
Compare color against approved samples or specified standards.
Check for uniform color distribution, avoiding gradients or patches.
Inspect texture patterns (e.g., leather grain, haircell) for uniform depth and spacing.
Verify consistent gloss or matte level throughout the part.
Note any streaks or swirls that may indicate poor material mixing.
Ensure gate vestiges are properly trimmed and flush with the surface as per design.
Check that runner and sprue cut-off points are free of excessive material.
Confirm no sink marks or voids caused by material removal at these areas.
Inspect for stress whitening or micro-cracks around the gate/runner/sprue regions.
Pin marks should be minimal, shallow, and evenly distributed.
Confirm no surface distortion or loss of functionality due to ejection forces.
Look for stress whitening or indentations from ejection pins.
Ensure no gouges or raised areas caused by incorrect ejection.
Place the part on a flat surface to detect bending, twisting, or warping.
Check critical planes and reference features for straightness and stability.
Verify thickness uniformity to prevent localized warpage.
Pay close attention to complex geometries (ribs, bosses) prone to distortion.
Inspect holes and slots for correct size, shape, and freedom from blockages.
Verify threads are clean, well-formed, and allow easy engagement.
Test snap-fits, latches for proper function without damage.
Ensure bosses and ribs are correctly formed and positioned for assembly or support.
If feasible, perform a dry-fit with mating parts to confirm correct alignment.
Ensure text, logos, part numbers, and symbols are legible, correctly spelled, and properly oriented.
Check that engraved or embossed features have uniform depth and clarity.
No forcing parts. They should fit smoothly without bending or leaving large gaps.
Align holes, pegs, marks, and reference features correctly. Ensure each part faces the right direction.
Brackets and mounts must hold components securely at the correct angles.
Use the correct type, size, and length of screws, bolts, or rivets.
Tighten fasteners to the recommended torque - neither too loose nor too tight.
Snap-fits and clips should click smoothly into place without cracking.
Apply adhesives, tapes, or sealants evenly, without excess material blocking movement or appearing on visible surfaces.
Hinges, sliders, and pivots must move freely. Lubricate if required.
Keep wiring neat, without tangles, pinching, or contact with sharp edges.
Ensure all connectors are fully plugged in and locked, with no loose wires.
Leave some slack so wires aren't stretched. Use strain relief where needed.
Test doors, knobs, lids, hinges, and switches as you install them. They should operate smoothly and return to their original positions.
No interference: Moving parts must not rub or collide with other components.
Ensure no stray tools, screws, washers, or debris remain inside the product.
If the product is powered, do a brief test: Lights on? Motor runs quietly? Display works?
Operate controls (buttons, switches, knobs) again with everything assembled. They should still feel solid and respond correctly.
Check all visible surfaces for a consistent finish (color, texture, gloss). No major scratches, dents, or paint chips.
Wipe off dust, fingerprints, or smudges.
Logos, labels, and stickers should be straight, correctly placed, and not peeling.
Panels and edges should line up evenly, with no large gaps.
If size matters (e.g., fitting into a certain space), measure with a ruler or caliper to confirm correct dimensions.
All parts listed in the BOM must be present and accounted for.
Include any optional or customer-specific extras (filters, cables, attachments) as required.
Test child locks, emergency stops, or other safety features to ensure they engage and release properly.
Listen for unusual rattles, squeaks, or grinding. The product should run smoothly and quietly.
If mild vibration is expected, it should be within normal limits and not indicate something off-balance.
Gently tilt or move the product to ensure nothing loosens or rattles.
If conditions like temperature/humidity matter, ensure product can operate under these normal conditions.
If ready to pack, ensure the product is protected with foam inserts, bubble wrap, or other cushioning.
Include user manuals, warranty cards, compliance labels, and any required documentation.
Check external packaging labels, barcodes, and shipping marks for accuracy.
Note down any issues and how they were fixed. If something remains unresolved, report it to the appropriate team.
Sign off the checklist once confident everything meets the required standards. Keep the completed checklist for quality records.
